title: What is déjà vu? What is déjà vu? - Michael Molina
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】什麼是似曾相識？什麼是似曾相識？ ——麥可‧莫利納（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Have you experienced déjà vu?
cues.en: Have you experienced déjà vu?
cues.zh: 曾對生活中的場景產生既視感嗎？

cues.text: It's that shadowy feeling you get when a situation seems familiar.
cues.en: It's that shadowy feeling you get when a situation seems familiar.
cues.zh: 身邊出現的人事物隱約地 讓你感到似曾相識

cues.text: A scene in a restaurant plays out exactly as you remember.
cues.en: A scene in a restaurant plays out exactly as you remember.
cues.zh: 讓你感到似曾相識 例如餐廳內出現一個場景 和你記憶中某個片段不謀而合

cues.text: The world moves like a ballet you've choreographed, but the sequence can't be based on a past experience
cues.en: The world moves like a ballet you've choreographed, but the sequence can't be based on a past experience
cues.zh: 和你記憶中某個片段不謀而合 像整個世界跳起了芭蕾 而你就是編舞者 但你對這一切毫無經驗 因為你從未在這裡吃過飯

cues.text: because you've never eaten here before.
cues.en: because you've never eaten here before.
cues.zh: 因為你從未在這裡吃過飯

cues.text: This is the first time you've had clams, so what's going on?
cues.en: This is the first time you've had clams, so what's going on?
cues.zh: 在這之前你也沒嘗過蛤蜊 究竟是怎麼回事？

cues.text: Unfortunately, there isn't one single explanation for déjà vu.
cues.en: Unfortunately, there isn't one single explanation for déjà vu.
cues.zh: 究竟是怎麼回事？ 可惜目前無法完整解釋這個現象

cues.text: The experience is brief and occurs without notice, making it nearly impossible for scientists to record and study it.
cues.en: The experience is brief and occurs without notice, making it nearly impossible for scientists to record and study it.
cues.zh: 這感覺來得快 去得也快 使得科學家幾乎無法 記錄並研究它

cues.text: Scientists can't simply sit around and wait for it to happen to them -- this could take years.
cues.en: Scientists can't simply sit around and wait for it to happen to them -- this could take years.
cues.zh: 總不能讓科學家整天不事生產 靜待生活中出現似曾相識的場景 說不定得花上數年光陰

cues.text: It has no physical manifestations and in studies, it's described by the subject as a sensation or feeling.
cues.en: It has no physical manifestations and in studies, it's described by the subject as a sensation or feeling.
cues.zh: 說不定得花上數年光陰 沒有具體的證據 人們也總是把這現象歸類為 一種感官上的知覺

cues.text: Because of this lack of hard evidence, there's been a surplus of speculation over the years.
cues.en: Because of this lack of hard evidence, there's been a surplus of speculation over the years.
cues.zh: 正因為沒有鐵證 多年來充斥著各式臆測

cues.text: Since Emile Boirac introduced déjà vu as a French term meaning "already seen,"
cues.en: Since Emile Boirac introduced déjà vu as a French term meaning "already seen,"
cues.zh: 自從法國科學家艾米爾．布拉克 將既視感定義為似曾相識起

cues.text: more than 40 theories attempt to explain this phenomenon.
cues.en: more than 40 theories attempt to explain this phenomenon.
cues.zh: 將既視感定義為似曾相識起 超過 40 種理論希望能 解釋這個現象

cues.text: Still, recent advancements in neuroimaging and cognitive psychology
cues.en: Still, recent advancements in neuroimaging and cognitive psychology
cues.zh: 然而近來神經造影以及 認知心理學的發達限縮了

cues.text: narrow down the field of prospects.
cues.en: narrow down the field of prospects.
cues.zh: 認知心理學的發達限縮了 既視感成因的可能性

cues.text: Let's walk through three of today's more prevalent theories, using the same restaurant setting for each.
cues.en: Let's walk through three of today's more prevalent theories, using the same restaurant setting for each.
cues.zh: 讓我們來瞧瞧 三種目前最普遍的說法吧 皆套用前面餐廳的假設

cues.text: First up is dual processing.
cues.en: First up is dual processing.
cues.zh: 首先是雙歷程理論

cues.text: We'll need an action.
cues.en: We'll need an action.
cues.zh: 首先是雙歷程理論 用一個動作來解釋

cues.text: Let's go with a waiter dropping a tray of dishes.
cues.en: Let's go with a waiter dropping a tray of dishes.
cues.zh: 用一個動作來解釋 服務生打翻了一堆碗盤

cues.text: As the scene unfolds, your brain's hemispheres process a flurry of information:
cues.en: As the scene unfolds, your brain's hemispheres process a flurry of information:
cues.zh: 服務生打翻了一堆碗盤 隨著畫面出現 你的大腦開始處理 一連串的資訊

cues.text: the waiter's flailing arms, his cry for help, the smell of pasta.
cues.en: the waiter's flailing arms, his cry for help, the smell of pasta.
cues.zh: 服務生揮舞雙臂 他大聲求援 義大利麵的香味

cues.text: Within milliseconds, this information zips through pathways and is processed into a single moment.
cues.en: Within milliseconds, this information zips through pathways and is processed into a single moment.
cues.zh: 在千分之一秒內 這個訊息快速穿梭於大腦中 最後合為一個瞬間的動作

cues.text: Most of the time, everything is recorded in-sync.
cues.en: Most of the time, everything is recorded in-sync.
cues.zh: 最後合為一個瞬間的動作 大腦通常會同步記錄訊息

cues.text: However, this theory asserts that déjà vu occurs when there's a slight delay
cues.en: However, this theory asserts that déjà vu occurs when there's a slight delay
cues.zh: 然而這個理論主張 若有資訊在腦中出現了些微延誤

cues.text: in information from one of these pathways.
cues.en: in information from one of these pathways.
cues.zh: 既視感便油然而生

cues.text: The difference in arrival times causes the brain to interpret the late information
cues.en: The difference in arrival times causes the brain to interpret the late information
cues.zh: 既視感便油然而生 訊息抵達的時間差 使大腦將前後的資訊解讀成 不同的事件

cues.text: as a separate event.
cues.en: as a separate event.
cues.zh: 不同的事件

cues.text: When it plays over the already-recorded moment, it feels as if it's happened before
cues.en: When it plays over the already-recorded moment, it feels as if it's happened before
cues.zh: 當大腦播放已存在的記憶 感覺就像發生過了一樣

cues.text: because, in a sense, it has.
cues.en: because, in a sense, it has.
cues.zh: 感覺就像發生過了一樣 某種情況而言，的確如此

cues.text: Our next theory deals with a confusion of the past rather than a mistake in the present.
cues.en: Our next theory deals with a confusion of the past rather than a mistake in the present.
cues.zh: 下個理論與記憶的混淆有關 而非當下的錯誤

cues.text: This is the hologram theory, and we'll use that tablecloth to examine it.
cues.en: This is the hologram theory, and we'll use that tablecloth to examine it.
cues.zh: 這就是全息理論 我們用這張桌布來檢視它

cues.text: As you scan its squares, a distant memory swims up from deep within your brain.
cues.en: As you scan its squares, a distant memory swims up from deep within your brain.
cues.zh: 你細看上頭的格紋 一段模糊的回憶 從大腦深處浮現

cues.text: According to the theory, this is because memories are stored in the form of holograms,
cues.en: According to the theory, this is because memories are stored in the form of holograms,
cues.zh: 從大腦深處浮現 根據這個理論 記憶在腦中是以 全息圖的形式儲存

cues.text: and in holograms, you only need one fragment to see the whole picture.
cues.en: and in holograms, you only need one fragment to see the whole picture.
cues.zh: 在全息圖中 只需要一小部分 便能窺見全域性 你的大腦認出了這張桌布

cues.text: Your brain has identified the tablecloth with one from the past, maybe from your grandmother's house.
cues.en: Your brain has identified the tablecloth with one from the past, maybe from your grandmother's house.
cues.zh: 你的大腦認出了這張桌布 好像以前看過 也許和奶奶家裡的是同一張 然而你並沒有想起

cues.text: However, instead of remembering that you've seen it at your grandmother's,
cues.en: However, instead of remembering that you've seen it at your grandmother's,
cues.zh: 然而你並沒有想起 你在奶奶家中見過這花色 大腦喚起了一段久遠的記憶

cues.text: your brain has summoned up the old memory without identifying it.
cues.en: your brain has summoned up the old memory without identifying it.
cues.zh: 大腦喚起了一段久遠的記憶 但是渾然不覺 這讓你產生強烈的熟悉感

cues.text: This leaves you stuck with familiarity, but no recollection.
cues.en: This leaves you stuck with familiarity, but no recollection.
cues.zh: 這讓你產生強烈的熟悉感 卻毫無記憶

cues.text: Although you've never been in this restaurant, you've seen that tablecloth but are just failing to identify it.
cues.en: Although you've never been in this restaurant, you've seen that tablecloth but are just failing to identify it.
cues.zh: 雖然你未曾來到這間餐廳 卻看過那張桌布 可是怎麼也想不起來

cues.text: Now, look at this fork.
cues.en: Now, look at this fork.
cues.zh: 接下來看看這把叉子

cues.text: Are you paying attention?
cues.en: Are you paying attention?
cues.zh: 接下來看看這把叉子 全神貫注了嗎？

cues.text: Our last theory is divided attention, and it states that déjà vu occurs
cues.en: Our last theory is divided attention, and it states that déjà vu occurs
cues.zh: 最後是分散性專注力理論 本理論主張既視感發生於

cues.text: when our brain subliminally takes in an environment while we're distracted by one particular object.
cues.en: when our brain subliminally takes in an environment while we're distracted by one particular object.
cues.zh: 本理論主張既視感發生於 大腦下意識接受了外在環境 但同時我們也分心在某個物件上

cues.text: When our attention returns, we feel as if we've been here before.
cues.en: When our attention returns, we feel as if we've been here before.
cues.zh: 但同時我們也分心在某個物件上 當注意力回歸時 我們對環境感到似曾相識

cues.text: For example, just now you focused on the fork and didn't observe the tablecloth or the falling waiter.
cues.en: For example, just now you focused on the fork and didn't observe the tablecloth or the falling waiter.
cues.zh: 例如剛才你正專注地盯著叉子 完全沒有注意到桌布 以及跌倒的服務生

cues.text: Although your brain has been recording everything in your peripheral vision,
cues.en: Although your brain has been recording everything in your peripheral vision,
cues.zh: 雖說你的大腦以邊緣視野 悄悄記錄了一切 那都在不被察覺的狀況下進行

cues.text: it's been doing so below conscious awareness.
cues.en: it's been doing so below conscious awareness.
cues.zh: 那都在不被察覺的狀況下進行

cues.text: When you finally pull yourself away from the fork, you think you've been here before because you have,
cues.en: When you finally pull yourself away from the fork, you think you've been here before because you have,
cues.zh: 那都在不被察覺的狀況下進行 當你把注意力 從叉子上移開 你會以為你曾經來過這裡 事實正是如此 只是你沒注意到罷了

cues.text: you just weren't paying attention.
cues.en: you just weren't paying attention.
cues.zh: 只是你沒注意到罷了 儘管以上三種理論

cues.text: While all three of these theories share the common features of déjà vu, none of them propose to be the conclusive source
cues.en: While all three of these theories share the common features of déjà vu, none of them propose to be the conclusive source
cues.zh: 儘管以上三種理論 皆掌握了既視感的特點 卻沒有任何一個能代表 既視感出現的決定性因素

cues.text: of the phenomenon.
cues.en: of the phenomenon.
cues.zh: 既視感出現的決定性因素

cues.text: Still, while we wait for researchers and inventers to come up with new ways to capture this fleeting moment,
cues.en: Still, while we wait for researchers and inventers to come up with new ways to capture this fleeting moment,
cues.zh: 然而我們期待研究員與發明家 能提出更好的方法 來捕捉這稍縱即逝的瞬間

cues.text: we can study the moment ourselves.
cues.en: we can study the moment ourselves.
cues.zh: 來捕捉這稍縱即逝的瞬間 我們也能自行研究此現象

cues.text: After all, most studies of déjà vu are based on first-hand accounts, so why can't one be yours?
cues.en: After all, most studies of déjà vu are based on first-hand accounts, so why can't one be yours?
cues.zh: 畢竟大多既視感的研究 都來自第一手資料 何不把你的經驗分享出來？

cues.text: The next time you get déjà vu, take a moment to think about it.
cues.en: The next time you get déjà vu, take a moment to think about it.
cues.zh: 何不把你的經驗分享出來？ 當既視感再度出現時 花點時間想想 你是否分心了？

cues.text: Have you been distracted?
cues.en: Have you been distracted?
cues.zh: 你是否分心了？ 四周有沒有熟悉的景物？

cues.text: Is there a familiar object somewhere?
cues.en: Is there a familiar object somewhere?
cues.zh: 四周有沒有熟悉的景物？ 大腦突然慢了半拍？

cues.text: Is your brain just acting slow?
cues.en: Is your brain just acting slow?
cues.zh: 大腦突然慢了半拍？ 還是…另有其因？

cues.text: Or is it something else?
cues.en: Or is it something else?
cues.zh: 還是…另有其因？
